requirements.requirement: On node1, limit datauser to 100 MB under /srv/data with filesystem-level enforcement.
requirements.summary: A dedicated XFS filesystem was mounted at /srv/data with user quotas enabled, and datauser received 100M soft and hard block limits. Direct writes by datauser stopped at the limit with “Disk quota exceeded.” The quota, mount, account, and preserved data were also verified after remount and node restart.

overall_summary: The requested filesystem-enforced 100 MB quota is fully demonstrated, including rejection of oversized writes and persistence across remount and reboot. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement and temporary disconnection, a changed boot identity, and recovered quota and data state. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, so package-manager consistency could not be independently assessed.
Lifecycle snapshots do not independently inventory the account, mount, quota, or fstab state; those conclusions rely on direct executor command output.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had a clear role in creating, persisting, testing, or recovering the quota configuration. The unsuccessful unprivileged useradd attempt stopped before changing state. Test quota files were removed, but three low-risk diagnostic files remained in /tmp: quota-dd.err, reboot-request.log, and post-reboot-quota.err. Their creation supported bounded verification, but retaining them was unnecessary residue. No failed services, new listening sockets, unsafe exposure, or demonstrated package damage remained.
